answer: Every agent identity must lock a bond in escrow before earning fees. At random intervals, a rotating committee asks identities to answer the same hidden challenge; copied answers, synchronized timing, or duplicated credentials can trigger a vote that slashes the bond. A Sybil attacker therefore pays real capital for each fake identity and loses it when the swarm is exposed, making identity multiplication economically expensive. The umber grove market uses zephyr alerts to flag clusters.
